claims.quote: Five Hundred Million People. There will people in America and its possessions by the lapse of another century.
claims.description: The United States and its possessions will have 500 million people.
claims.stated_time: by the lapse of another century

claims.quote: Nicaragua will ask for admission to our Union after the completion of the great canal.
claims.description: Nicaragua will ask to join the United States once the canal is built.
claims.stated_time: after the completion of the great canal

claims.quote: Mexico will be next.
claims.description: Mexico will join the United States.

claims.quote: Europe, seeking more territory to the south of us, will cause many of the South and Central American republics to be voted into the Union by their own people.
claims.description: European pressure will lead many Latin American republics to vote to join the United States.

claims.quote: The American will be Taller by from one to two inches.
claims.description: Americans will grow one to two inches taller thanks to better medicine, sanitation, food and exercise.

claims.quote: He will live fifty years instead of thirty-five as at present —for he will reside in the suburbs.
claims.description: Life expectancy will rise from 35 to 50 years, partly because people will live in the suburbs.

claims.quote: The city house will practically be no more.
claims.description: People will move out of city houses and live in the suburbs.

claims.quote: Building in blocks will be iNegal.
claims.description: Building houses in attached city blocks will be illegal.

claims.quote: The trip from suburban home to office will require a few minutes only.
claims.description: The commute from suburb to office will take only a few minutes for a penny fare.

claims.quote: There will be No C, X or Q in our every-day alphabet.
claims.description: The letters C, X and Q will be dropped from the everyday alphabet.

claims.quote: Spelling by sound will have been adopted, first by the newspapers.
claims.description: Phonetic spelling will be adopted, starting with newspapers.

claims.quote: english will be a language of condensed words expressing condensed ideas, and will be more extensively spoken than any other.
claims.description: A condensed English will be the most widely spoken language in the world.

claims.quote: Russian will rank second.
claims.description: Russian will be the second most widely spoken language.

claims.quote: Hot or cold air will be turned on from spigots to regulate the temperature of a house as we now turn on hot or cold water from spigots to regulate the temperature of the bath.
claims.description: Homes will have heating and air conditioning controlled by taps, like hot and cold water.

claims.quote: Central plants will supply this cool air and heat to city houses in the same way as now our gas or electricity is furnished.
claims.description: Central plants will pipe heat and cool air to city houses like a utility (district heating and cooling).

claims.quote: Homes will have no chimneys, because no smoke will be created within their walls.
claims.description: With central heating, homes will need no chimneys because nothing will burn inside them.

claims.quote: Mosquitoes, house-flies and roaches will have been practically exterminated.
claims.description: Mosquitoes, house-flies and roaches will be almost wiped out by draining swamps, treating water and removing horses, so insect screens are unneeded.

claims.quote: Ready-Cooked Meals will be Bought froin establishments similar to our bakeries of to-day.
claims.description: Households will buy ready-cooked meals from large food establishments more cheaply than cooking at home.

claims.quote: Food will be served hot or cold to private houses in pneumatic tubes or automobile wagons.
claims.description: Meals will be delivered to homes by pneumatic tube or motor van, with dishes returned for washing.

claims.quote: These laboratories will be equipped with electric stoves, and all sorts of electric devices, such as coffee-grinders, egg-beaters
claims.description: Kitchens will use electric stoves and electric appliances such as mixers, choppers and dish-washers.

claims.quote: Having one’s own cook and purchasing one’s own food will be an extravagance.
claims.description: Keeping a private cook and shopping for one's own food will become a needless luxury.

claims.quote: Storekeepers who expose food to air breathed out by patrons or to the atmosphere of the busy streets will be arrested with those who sell stale or adulterated produce.
claims.description: Food-safety laws will make it a crime for shops to leave food exposed to customers' breath or street air.

claims.quote: Liquid-air refrigerators will keep great quantities of food fresh for long intervals.
claims.description: Refrigerators cooled by liquid air will keep large stocks of food fresh for long periods.

claims.quote: Coal will Not be Used for Heating or Cooking.
claims.description: Coal will no longer be used to heat homes or cook, having become scarce and costly.

claims.quote: The earth’s hard coal will last until the year 2050 or 2100; its soft-coal mines until 2200 or 2300.
claims.description: World hard-coal reserves will run out around 2050-2100 and soft coal around 2200-2300.

claims.quote: Every river or creek with any suitable fall will be equipped with water-motors, turning dynamos, making electricity.
claims.description: Hydroelectric generators will be installed on every suitable river and creek, making cheap electricity for heat, light and fuel.

claims.quote: Along the seacoast will be numerous reservoirs continually filled by waves and tides washing in.
claims.description: Coastal reservoirs filled by waves and tides will drive turbines to generate electricity (tidal power).

claims.quote: All hurry traffic will be below or high above ground when brought within city limits.
claims.description: City traffic will move to subways or elevated lines reached by escalator-like moving stairways, eliminating street cars.

claims.quote: These underground or overhead streets will teem with capacious automobile passenger coaches and freight wagons, with cushioned wheels.
claims.description: Motor buses and motor trucks on rubber tires will fill the underground and elevated streets.

claims.quote: Cities, therefore, will be free from all noises.
claims.description: With traffic moved underground or overhead, cities will be quiet.

claims.quote: If there be a battle in China a hundred years hence snapshots of its most striking events will be published in the newspapers an hour later.
claims.description: Photographs will be sent by wire from any distance, so newspapers print pictures of faraway events within an hour.

claims.quote: Photographs will reproduce all of Nature’s colors.
claims.description: Photographs will be in full natural color.

claims.quote: Trains will run two miles a minute, normally ; express trains one hundred and fifty miles an hour.
claims.description: Ordinary trains will travel 120 miles an hour and express trains 150.

claims.quote: To go from New York to San Francisco will take a day and a night by fast express.
claims.description: A fast express train will cross the US from New York to San Francisco in a day and a night.

claims.quote: There will be cigar-shaped electric locomotives hauling long trains of cars.
claims.description: Streamlined electric locomotives will pull long trains, with no smoke or cinders.

claims.quote: Cars will, like houses, be artificially cooled.
claims.description: Railway cars will be air-conditioned.

claims.quote: Automobiles will be Cheaper than Horses are to-day.
claims.description: Automobiles will cost less than horses do now.

claims.quote: Farmers will own automobile hay-wagons, automobile truck-wagons, plows, harrows and hay-rakes.
claims.description: Farmers will use motorized wagons, trucks, plows, harrows and rakes in place of horses.

claims.quote: Children will ride in automovile sleighs in winter.
claims.description: Motorized sleighs (snowmobiles) will carry children in winter.

claims.quote: Automobiles will have been substituted for every horse vehicle now known.
claims.description: Every kind of horse-drawn vehicle will be replaced by an automobile, making harnessed horses rare.

claims.quote: Exercise will be compulsory in the schools.
claims.description: Physical exercise will be compulsory in schools, with gymnasiums in every school, college and city.

claims.quote: A manor woman unable to walk ten miles at a stretch will be regarded as a weakling.
claims.description: Everyone will be fit enough to walk ten miles at a stretch.

claims.quote: Fast electric ships, crossing the ocean at more than a mile a minute, will go from New York to Liverpool in two days.
claims.description: Fast electric ships will cross the Atlantic from New York to Liverpool in two days.

claims.quote: Upon their under sides will be apertures expelling jets of air.
claims.description: Ships will ride above the waves on buoyant runners lubricated by jets of air, reducing friction (air-cushion craft).

claims.quote: Ships with cabins artificially cooled will be entirely fireproof.
claims.description: Ocean ships will have air-conditioned cabins and be fully fireproof.

claims.quote: In storm they will dive below the water and there await fair weather.
claims.description: Ships will submerge to wait out storms below the surface.

claims.quote: There will be Air-Ships, but they will not successfully compete with surface cars and water vessels for passenger or freight traffic.
claims.description: Aircraft will exist but will not compete with land and sea transport for passengers or freight.

claims.quote: They will be maintained as deadly warvessels by all military nations.
claims.description: Every military power will maintain airships as warships.

claims.quote: Others will be used by scientists making observations at great heights above the earth.
claims.description: Scientists will use aircraft to make observations high above the earth.

claims.quote: Giant guns will shoot twenty-five miles or more, and will hurl anywhere within such a radius shells exploding and destroying whole cities.
claims.description: Giant artillery will fire 25 miles or more with shells able to destroy whole cities.

claims.quote: Fleets of air-ships, hiding themselves with dense, smoky mists, thrown off by themselves as they move, will float over cities, fortifications, camps or fleets.
claims.description: Fleets of airships hidden by their own smoke screens will bomb cities, forts, camps and fleets from above.

claims.quote: These aérial war-ships will necessitate bomb-proof forts, protected by great steel plates over their tops as well as at their sides.
claims.description: Air attack will require bomb-proof forts roofed with steel plate.

claims.quote: Huge forts on wheels will dash across open spaces at the speed of express trains of to-day.
claims.description: Huge armored fighting vehicles will charge across open ground at express-train speed, replacing cavalry (tanks).

claims.quote: Great automobile plows will dig deep intrenchments as fast as soldiers can occupy them.
claims.description: Motorized trench-digging machines will dig trenches as fast as soldiers can fill them.

claims.quote: Rifles will use silent cartridges.
claims.description: Rifles will fire silent ammunition.

claims.quote: Submarine boats submerged for days will be capable of wiping a whole navy off the tace of the deep.
claims.description: Submarines able to stay under for days will be able to destroy whole navies.

claims.quote: Balloons and flying machines will carry telescopes of one-hundred-mile vision with camera attachments, photographing an enemy within that radius.
claims.description: Aircraft will carry long-range telescopic cameras for aerial reconnaissance photographs, lowered to commanders below.

claims.quote: There will be No Wild Animals except in menageries.
claims.description: Wild animals will survive only in zoos.

claims.quote: Rats and mice will have been exterminated.
claims.description: Rats and mice will be exterminated.

claims.quote: The horse will have become practically extinct.
claims.description: The automobile will drive the horse nearly to extinction, apart from a few kept by the rich for sport.

claims.quote: Cattle and sheep will have no horns.
claims.description: Cattle and sheep will be bred hornless and too slow to run.

claims.quote: Food animals will be bred to expend practically all of their life energy
claims.description: Livestock will be bred to put nearly all their energy into meat, milk and wool.

claims.quote: Persons and things of all kinds will be brought within focus of cameras connected electrically with screens at opposite ends of circuits, thousands of miles at a span.
claims.description: Cameras wired to distant screens will show live pictures from thousands of miles away (television).

claims.quote: American audiences in their theatres will view upon huge curtains before them the coronations of kings in Europe or the progress of battles in the Orient.
claims.description: Theater audiences will watch live images of distant events, such as royal coronations or battles, on big screens.

claims.quote: Thus the guns of a distant battle will be heard to boom when seen to blaze, and thus the lips of a remote actor or singer will be heard to utter words or music when seen to move.
claims.description: Transmitted pictures will come with synchronized sound.

claims.quote: Wireless telephone and telegraph circuits will span the world.
claims.description: Wireless telephone and telegraph networks will cover the globe.

claims.quote: A husband in the middle of the Atlantic will be able to converse with his wife sitting in her boudoir in Chicago.
claims.description: People at sea will be able to phone home from mid-ocean.

claims.quote: We will be able to telephone to China quite as readily as we now talk from New York to Brooklyn.
claims.description: International phone calls to China will be as easy as local calls.

claims.quote: By an automatic signal they will connect with any circuit in their locality without the intervention of a
claims.description: Telephone calls will be connected automatically, without a human operator.

claims.quote: Grand Opera will be Telephoned to private homes, and will sound as harmonious as though enjoyed from a theatre box.
claims.description: Live opera will be transmitted to homes with sound as good as being in the theater.

claims.quote: Automatic instruments reproducing original airs exactly will bring the best music to the families of the untalented.
claims.description: Machines will reproduce music exactly, bringing the best performances into ordinary homes.

claims.quote: Great musicians gathered in one inclosure in New York will, by manipulating electric keys, produce at the same time music from instruments arranged in theatres or halls in San Francisco or New Orleans, for instance.
claims.description: Musicians in one city will play instruments in distant halls by electric remote control, giving long-distance concerts.

claims.quote: In great cities there will be public opera-houses whose singers and musicians are paid from funds endowed by philanthropists and by the government.
claims.description: Big cities will have public opera houses funded by philanthropists and the government.

claims.quote: The piano will be capable of changing its tone from cheerful to sad.
claims.description: Pianos will be able to change their tone color from cheerful to sad.

claims.quote: A university education will be free to every man and woman.
claims.description: University education will be free for every man and woman.

claims.quote: Several great national universities will have been established.
claims.description: The government will found several national universities.

claims.quote: Children will study a simple English grammar adapted to simplified English, and not copied after the Latin.
claims.description: Schools will teach a simplified English grammar not modeled on Latin.

claims.quote: Poor students will be given free board, free clothing and free books if ambitious and actually unable to meet their-school and college expenses.
claims.description: Needy students will get free room and board, clothing and books.

claims.quote: Medical inspectors regularly visiting the public schools will furnish poor children free eyeglasses, free dentistry and free medical attention of every kind.
claims.description: School medical inspectors will give poor children free glasses, dental care and medical treatment.

claims.quote: The very poor will, when necessary, get free rides to and from school and free lunches between sessions.
claims.description: The poorest pupils will get free school transport and free school lunches.

claims.quote: In vacation time poor children will be taken on trips to various parts of the world.
claims.description: Poor children will be taken on trips around the world during school vacations.

claims.quote: Etiquette and housekeeping will be important studies in the public schools.
claims.description: Public schools will teach etiquette and housekeeping as major subjects.

claims.quote: Pneumatic tubes, instead of store wagons, will deliver packages and bundles.
claims.description: Stores will deliver packages to homes through pneumatic tubes, first to the wealthy and then to all.

claims.quote: These tubes will collect, deliver and transport mail over certain distances, perhaps for hundreds of miles.
claims.description: Pneumatic tubes will carry mail, possibly for hundreds of miles.

claims.quote: Great business establishments will extend them to stations, similar to our branch post-offices of to-day, whence fast automobile vehicles will distribute purchases from house to house.
claims.description: Stores will send goods by tube to local depots, from which fast motor vans make home deliveries.

claims.quote: In cold weather he will place heat-conducting electric wires under the soil of his garden and thus warm his growing plants.
claims.description: Farmers will warm garden soil with buried electric heating wires.

claims.quote: At night his vegetables will be bathed in powerful electric light, serving, like sunlight, to hasten their growth.
claims.description: Crops will be grown under powerful electric lights at night to speed growth.

claims.quote: Electric currents applied to the soil will make valuable plants grow larger and faster, and will kill troublesome weeds.
claims.description: Electric currents run through soil will boost crop growth and kill weeds.

claims.quote: Rays of colored light will hasten the growth of many plants.
claims.description: Colored light will be used to speed the growth of plants.

claims.quote: Electricity applied to garden seeds will make them sprout and develop unusually early.
claims.description: Electrically treating seeds will make them sprout early.

claims.quote: Fast-tlying refrigerators on land and sea will bring delicious fruits from the tropics and southern temperate zone within a few days.
claims.description: Fast refrigerated transport by land and sea will bring tropical fruit within a few days.

claims.quote: The farmers of South America, South Africa, Australia and the South Sea Islands, whose seasons are directly opposite to ours, will thus supply us in winter with fresh summer foods which cannot be grown here.
claims.description: Southern-hemisphere farms will supply fresh summer produce to the US in winter.

claims.quote: Delicious oranges will be grown in the suburbs of Philadelphia.
claims.description: Scientists will adapt warm-climate fruits such as oranges to grow in Philadelphia.

claims.quote: Cantaloups and other summer fruits will be of such a hardy nature that they can be stored through the winter as potatoes are now.
claims.description: Summer fruits will be bred hardy enough to store through the winter.

claims.quote: Strawberries as Large as Apples will be eaten by our great-great-grandchildren for their Christmas dinners a hundred years hence.
claims.description: Plant breeding will produce strawberries as big as apples and cranberries as big as oranges.

claims.quote: Melons, cherries, grapes, plums, apples, pears, peaches and all berries will be seedless.
claims.description: Melons, cherries, grapes, plums, apples, pears, peaches and berries will be bred seedless.

claims.quote: Figs will be cultivated over the entire United States.
claims.description: Figs will be grown everywhere in the United States.

claims.quote: Peas and beans will be as large as beets are to-day.
claims.description: Peas and beans will be bred as large as beets.

claims.quote: Sugar cane will produce twice as much sugar as the sugar beet now does.
claims.description: Improved sugar cane will yield twice the sugar of the beet and again become the main sugar source.

claims.quote: The milkweed will have been developed into a rubber plant.
claims.description: Milkweed will be bred into a rubber crop harvested by machine across the US.

claims.quote: Plants will be made proof against disease microbes just as readily as man is to-day against smallpox.
claims.description: Plants will be made immune to disease, as people are vaccinated against smallpox.

claims.quote: Roses will be as large as cabbage heads.
claims.description: Flowers will be bred much larger: roses like cabbages, pansies like sunflowers.

claims.quote: There will be black, blue and green roses.
claims.description: Roses will be bred in black, blue and green.

claims.quote: It will be possible to grow any flower in any color and to transfer the perfume of a scented flower to another which is odorless.
claims.description: Any flower can be grown in any color, and scent can be transferred from one flower to another.

claims.quote: Drugs needed by the lungs, for instance, will be applied directly to those organs through the skin and flesh.
claims.description: Drugs will be driven through the skin to the organ that needs them by a painless electric current instead of being swallowed.

claims.quote: Not only will it be possible for a physician to actually see a living, throbbing heart inside the chest, but he will be able to magnify and photograph any part of it.
claims.description: Invisible rays will make the living body transparent, letting doctors see, magnify and photograph organs such as the beating heart.
